Non-fork subagents start with a fresh context; 'tools' and 'disallowedTools' frontmatter restrict tools. BUT fork mode is on by default (v2.1.302+, interactive from v2.1.232) and a fork inherits the entire conversation. This affects P200-173.

stdio: server MUST NOT write non-MCP data to stdout and MAY log to stderr. Streamable HTTP: server returns application/json or text/event-stream and the client MUST support both (SSE optional). Servers MUST validate Origin, SHOULD bind to localhost, SHOULD authenticate. Disconnect SHOULD NOT be treated as cancellation. HTTP+SSE is deprecated. P200-041..044, 048, 057..059 correct.

initialize -> initialized notification before normal operation; capability negotiation; no shutdown message is defined; request IDs MUST NOT be null; notifications MUST NOT have IDs. P200-045..047, 053..056 correct.

Tools are model-controlled, resources application-driven, prompts user-controlled; notifications/tools/list_changed; isError for tool execution errors; annotations are untrusted unless from trusted servers; a human SHOULD be able to deny invocations. P200-049..052, 055 correct.

flags.problem: The stem asks what to expect about subagent context 'by default', and the key says context is separate with no automatic sharing. Current docs say fork mode is ON by default (v2.1.302+) and a fork 'inherits the entire conversation so far'; only non-fork subagents start fresh. Distractor A ('every subagent automatically has all parent details') is still wrong because of 'every', but the 'by default' framing is no longer safe. Reword the stem to a custom subagent defined in .claude/agents/.

The stem says the service is bound to localhost. The most direct reason remote users cannot connect is that a loopback-bound socket accepts only local connections, but the key cites only DNS vs routing/firewall. The key is defensible, but it hides the real cause, and a test-taker who knows networking may find no option that names it.

The stem asks 'what versioning issue', but the key is an action. 'Migrate only compatible question records while preserving the old progress data' is internally unclear: does it preserve all old data or only compatible records? The point (stable content-keyed progress IDs) is never stated, so B and C partially overlap in concept.

Only PostToolUse is a plausible competitor: SessionEnd is obviously irrelevant, and D ('a final prose warning') is not a hook event. PermissionRequest (exists, but exit 2 is not honored there) or UserPromptSubmit would make this a real discrimination test.
Distractor B calls itself 'a fake flag ... invented by the model', which removes it as a choice. A and D are also implausible, so the item tests nothing beyond reading.
B ('Reuse approval after changing amount or recipient'), C and D are all restatements of 'don't re-approve'. With no competing plausible design, only A is left.
The stem asks 'which layer', but only A names a layer. B–D are absurd actions ('treat raw text as a high-priority instruction'), so a grammatical cue gives the answer away.
The key is the only diagnosis (noun phrase). A–C are absurd actions, so the item is answerable without JSON-RPC knowledge.

The cited structured-outputs page says constrained decoding guarantees valid JSON, which makes a trailing-comma failure moot. The item never offers structured outputs as the fix. The key (parse with a real parser) is fine generically, but the citation does not support the scenario, and an exam-aligned item would test the structured-outputs mechanism.

summary: All 200 items read. Every Claude-specific factual claim tested in the bank (stop reasons, tool_use/tool_result pairing and is_error, prompt-cache prefix order, streaming events, API error classes, Claude Code hooks/exit code 2, CLI flags -p/--output-format/--max-turns/--append-system-prompt/--json-schema, .claude/rules paths frontmatter, settings.local.json, subagent tools allowlist, SKILL.md, deny rules, worktrees, MCP stdio/Streamable HTTP/Origin/localhost/auth, lifecycle, JSON-RPC IDs/notifications, primitives, listChanged, isError) was checked against current official docs and holds. No keyed answer was found to be technically wrong. One item (P200-173) is now ambiguous because Claude Code fork mode, which inherits full parent context, is on by default. Two more items are ambiguous or poorly worded (P200-158, P200-187), and one is mis-filed by domain (P200-092). Five items have weak distractors. Eleven flagged items (covering about 17 items, counting the siblings noted in P200-157 and P200-185) cite sources that do not support their specific claims (citation mismatch; the content itself is correct general practice). Bank-level issues: (1) Answer cueing. The correct option is strictly the longest in 96/200 items (48%; chance is about 25%). In about 39 items the key is the only option containing a safeguard word (bounded, explicit, authorized, validate, reconcile, scope). Most distractors are deliberately unsafe or absurd, so an estimated majority of items can be answered by 'pick the safe, hedged option' without Claude knowledge. (2) Scope. About 26 items (listed in off_blueprint) cover a home-hosted study app, local GPU serving, fine-tuning/PEFT, TV-script licensing, humor, WCAG and the bank's own meta-status, which are unlikely to appear on CCA-F. (3) Coverage gaps. No items cover tool_choice, Message Batches, extended/adaptive thinking, the Agent SDK, MCP authorization (OAuth), MCP sampling/elicitation/roots, .mcp.json/MCP config in Claude Code, CLAUDE.md hierarchy/imports, plan mode, slash commands, citations, or strict tool use. Only about 77 items mention any Claude/MCP-specific term at all. (4) Redundancy clusters: 031/124/126 (uncertain write), 023/093 (ask for missing input), 021/035 (tool descriptions), 029/034/092/183 (authorization vs approval), 038/123 (transient retry). Not verified: OWASP, WCAG and Hugging Face content beyond URL resolution and topic fit; whether these topics match the official CCA-F blueprint (only third-party guides are public).
